items.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 24 at 6:32AM EST until November 26 at 4:00PM EST by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
items.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Areas along Bogue Banks beaches, Bogue Sound, the
Newport and White Oak Rivers, and adjacent tidal creeks, and
areas in North Topsail Beach, the lower New River, and
adjacent tidal creeks.

* WHEN...From Wednesday evening through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Up to 1 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level
is possible in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Isolated road closures and flooding of
vehicles will be possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King Tides will be peaking on Wednesday
and Thursday before gradually lowering which will continue to
bring elevated water levels to the area through much of the
week. The King Tides will be exacerbated by a strong coastal
low impacting the area Wednesday evening into Thursday
morning. The higher of the high tide cycles will be during the
morning hours each day this week. This is forecast to bring
nuisance water level rises on Tuesday across the watch area
with minor to locally moderate impacts forecast on Wednesday.
The worst impacts are currently forecast with the morning high
tide cycle on Thursday.
items.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

items.headline: Gale Warning issued November 24 at 4:22AM EST until November 26 at 9:00AM EST by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
items.description:
* WHAT...Northeast winds 25 to 35 kt with gusts up to 45 kt and
seas 10 to 15 ft expected.

* WHERE...The coastal waters from Cape Hatteras to Surf City.

* WHEN...Until 9 AM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
items.instruction:
Mariners should alter plans to avoid these hazardous conditions.
Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for hazardous conditions.
